definition_en: a thick liquid served with food to add flavour
core_image: 一勺浓稠的番茄酱浇在热气腾腾的意大利面上
scene: 厨房里，妈妈把酱汁浇在面条上。Mom poured the sauce over the noodles.
sceneCN: 这里 sauce 是「调味汁」（第 1 个义项）；句意：妈妈把酱汁浇在了面条上。

senses.title: Flavoured liquid
senses.definition: a thick liquid served with food to add flavour
senses.definitionCN: 与食物一起食用、用来增添风味的浓稠液体
senses.example: She made a rich tomato sauce for the pasta.
senses.exampleCN: 她为意面做了一份浓郁的番茄酱。
senses.why: The basic sense is a liquid that flavours food.
senses.whyCN: 基本义是给食物增添风味的液体。

senses.title: Cooking juices
senses.definition: the juice that comes from meat while it is cooking
senses.definitionCN: 肉在烹制过程中流出的汁液
senses.example: The roast beef was served with its own sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 烤牛肉配着它自身的肉汁一起上桌。
senses.why: Natural cooking juices work like a sauce.
senses.whyCN: 烹制时流出的天然汁液起着酱汁的作用。

senses.title: Audacity
senses.definition: rude or cheeky behaviour, used informally
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用语，指无礼或冒失的行为
senses.example: Nobody has the sauce to argue with her.
senses.exampleCN: 没人敢冒失地跟她争辩。
senses.why: The flavour image shifts to a bold and sharp manner.
senses.whyCN: 从味道的形象引申为大胆而带刺的态度。

intro.en: Sauce comes from Latin salsus, meaning salted, through Old French.
intro.cn: sauce 源自拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Salsus means salted, from sal, salt.
items.cn: salsus 意为盐腌的，来自 sal（盐）。

items.en: Salsa meant a salted or seasoned preparation.
items.cn: salsa 指盐腌或调味的食物。

items.en: Sauce named a seasoned liquid served with food.
items.cn: sauce 在古法语中指配食物的调味液体。

items.en: English borrowed sauce for liquid served with meat.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 sauce，指配肉食的液态调料。

items.en: Sauce now covers sweet, savoury, and figurative uses.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sauce 兼指甜酱、咸酱与引申义。

note.en: Sauce is compared with look-alike words and with other things served alongside food.
note.cn: 把 sauce 与形近词以及佐餐调料作比较。

entries.definition: a small shallow dish for a cup
a room filled with hot steam for bathing
to soak food in salty water

normalIntro.en: Sauce can be remembered by sound, image, and word family.
normalIntro.cn: 可以从读音、画面和词族三个角度记住 sauce。

normal.en: Think of sauce as the source of flavour on the plate.
normal.cn: 把 sauce 想成盘子里风味的来源，即 source。

normal.en: The round au in sauce looks like a drop of gravy.
normal.cn: sauce 中圆圆的 au 像一滴酱汁。

normal.en: Soy sauce and tomato sauce are two everyday examples.
normal.cn: 酱油和番茄酱是两个日常例子。

normal.en: Saucy means cheeky, just as sauce can mean audacity.
normal.cn: saucy 意为俏皮无礼，正如 sauce 可指冒失。

normal.en: The plural sauces simply adds s to the base word.
normal.cn: 复数 sauces 只需在词尾加 s。

abstract.en: Sauce is the seasoning that turns plain food into a treat.
abstract.cn: 酱汁是把普通食物变成美味的调味。

abstract.en: A little sauce can change the whole mood of a meal.
abstract.cn: 一点酱汁就能改变整顿饭的气氛。

abstract.en: Sauce hides neither the food nor itself; it blends both.
abstract.cn: 酱汁既不掩盖食物也不掩盖自己，而是让两者融合。

examples.en: The chef added a spoonful of sauce to the rice.
examples.cn: 厨师往米饭里加了一勺酱汁。

examples.en: Too much sauce can hide the taste of the fish.
examples.cn: 酱汁太多会盖住鱼的味道。

examples.en: She stirred the sauce slowly over low heat.
examples.cn: 她在小火上慢慢搅动酱汁。

dict_mnemonic.text: sauce 与 salt（盐）同源，最初指盐腌调味的液体，可记「一勺带咸香的酱汁」。

root: 源自拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的），经古法语 sauce 进入英语，核心义「加盐调味、配食物食用的液体」。

sensesIntro.en: Sauce means a flavoured liquid for food, natural cooking juices, or informally audacity.
sensesIntro.cn: sauce 意为给食物调味的液体、天然肉汁，或口语中的冒失无礼。

core.en: A seasoned liquid that adds flavour to food.
core.cn: 给食物增添风味的调味液体。

branches.en: The core sense, a flavoured liquid served with a dish.
branches.cn: 核心义，配菜食用的调味液体。

branches.en: Natural meat juices used as a sauce.
branches.cn: 用作酱汁的天然肉汁。

branches.en: Boldness, from spicy flavour to a sharp manner.
branches.cn: 由辛辣味道引申出的冒失态度。

branches.en: Everyday cooking links poured sauce and natural juices.
branches.cn: 日常烹饪把浇上的酱汁和天然肉汁联系起来。

branches.en: Rich juice and bold manner both suggest strength.
branches.cn: 浓郁的肉汁与大胆的态度都暗示强烈。

intro.en: Sauce belongs to a family of cooking and manner words.
intro.cn: sauce 属于一个兼指烹饪与态度的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin salsus, salted, is the distant source of sauce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的）是 sauce 的远源。

items.meaning: a deep pan with a long handle
items.example: Boil the water in a saucepan.

items.meaning: a rich egg and butter sauce

items.exampleCN: 他们用薯片蘸萨尔萨酱。

latinEntries.example: Sal is the root of salsus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sal 是 salsus 的词根。

definition_en: a small shallow dish on which a cup is placed
core_image: 早餐桌上，一只茶杯稳稳放在小圆碟上
scene: 早餐桌上，茶杯稳稳放在小碟上。The cup rests on a saucer.
sceneCN: 这里 saucer 是「茶托」（第 1 个义项）；句意：茶杯稳稳地放在茶托上。

collocations.phrase: place the cup on the saucer

senses.title: Dish under a cup
senses.definition: a small shallow dish on which a cup is placed
senses.definitionCN: 用来垫放茶杯的小浅碟
senses.example: She set the teacup back on its saucer.
senses.exampleCN: 她把茶杯放回茶托上。
senses.why: The core sense is the small plate that catches drips from a cup.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是承接杯中滴液的小碟子。

senses.title: Small shallow dish
senses.definition: any small shallow round dish used for serving
senses.definitionCN: 任何用于盛放食物的小浅圆盘
senses.example: The cat drank milk from a saucer.
senses.exampleCN: 猫从浅碟里喝牛奶。
senses.why: The cup dish extends to other small round dishes.
senses.whyCN: 垫杯的小碟扩展为其他小圆盘。

senses.title: Flying saucer
senses.definition: a disc-shaped object reported in the sky, in the phrase flying saucer
senses.definitionCN: 短语 flying saucer 中指天空中出现的碟状飞行物
senses.example: The boy said he saw a flying saucer.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩说他看见了一个飞碟。
senses.why: The round shape links a tea dish to a disc in the sky.
senses.whyCN: 圆盘形状把茶碟与天空中的碟状物联系起来。

intro.en: Saucer first meant a sauce dish, then shifted to the dish under a cup.
intro.cn: saucer 最初指盛酱汁的碟子，后来转指垫茶杯的小碟。

items.en: Salsus, salted, is the distant root shared with sauce.
items.cn: salsus（盐腌的）是与 sauce 共有的远源。

items.en: Sauciere named a vessel for serving sauce.
items.cn: sauciere 指盛放酱汁的器皿。

items.en: Saucer entered English as a small sauce dish.
items.cn: saucer 以「小酱碟」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word shifted to the shallow dish under a cup.
items.cn: 该词转指垫在茶杯下的浅碟。

items.en: Flying saucer extended the round shape to the sky.
items.cn: flying saucer 把圆盘形状引申到天空。

note.en: Saucer is compared with similar spellings and with other tableware.
note.cn: 把 saucer 与形近拼写和其他餐具作比较。

entries.definition: a hot steam room for bathing
to walk in a slow relaxed way
a flat round dish for food
a small mat under a glass

normalIntro.en: Saucer is sauce plus -er, once a dish for sauce.
normalIntro.cn: saucer 是 sauce 加 -er，原本指盛酱汁的碟子。

normal.en: A saucer is the small dish that catches sauce drips.
normal.cn: saucer 是接住酱汁滴落的小碟子。

normal.en: The spelling keeps sauce and adds er at the end.
normal.cn: 拼写保留 sauce，并在末尾加上 er。

normal.en: Cup and saucer always appear as a pair on the table.
normal.cn: 杯子和茶托在桌上总是成对出现。

normal.en: A flying saucer is a round object, like a tea dish.
normal.cn: 飞碟是圆形的，正像茶碟。

normal.en: Remember the phrase a saucer of milk for the cat.
normal.cn: 记住 a saucer of milk 这个给猫喝奶的搭配。

abstract.en: The saucer holds what the cup cannot keep.
abstract.cn: 茶托接住杯子留不住的东西。

abstract.en: A small dish can carry a large meaning in a tea ritual.
abstract.cn: 一只小碟在茶礼中承载着不小的意义。

abstract.en: The same round shape travels from table to sky.
abstract.cn: 同样的圆盘形状从餐桌走向天空。

examples.en: He placed the cup gently on the saucer.
examples.cn: 他把杯子轻轻放在茶托上。

examples.en: The saucer was cracked along one edge.
examples.cn: 茶碟的一边裂了。

examples.en: Children drew a flying saucer above the town.
examples.cn: 孩子们在小镇上空画了一个飞碟。

dict_mnemonic.text: saucer 由 sauce 加 -er 构成，原是盛酱汁的小碟，后来专指茶杯下的茶托。

root: 由 sauce 加 -er 构成，古法语 sauciere 指酱汁器皿，核心义「盛放酱汁或垫杯的小浅碟」。

sensesIntro.en: Saucer means the small dish under a cup, a shallow serving dish, or a flying disc.
sensesIntro.cn: saucer 意为茶杯下的小碟、盛食物的浅碟，或飞碟。

core.en: A small shallow dish linked to cups and sauce.
core.cn: 与茶杯和酱汁相关的小浅碟。

branches.en: The everyday dish under a teacup.
branches.cn: 日常垫在茶杯下的小碟。

branches.en: Any small shallow dish for food.
branches.cn: 任何盛食物的小浅碟。

branches.en: The disc shape in flying saucer.
branches.cn: 飞碟中的圆盘形状。

branches.en: Both are small round dishes used at the table.
branches.cn: 两者都是餐桌上使用的小圆碟。

branches.en: The round dish shape is reused for a sky object.
branches.cn: 圆碟形状被借用来指天空中的物体。

intro.en: Saucer shares its base with the sauce word family.
intro.cn: saucer 与 sauce 词族共享词基。

latinIntro.en: The family traces back to Latin salsus, salted.
latinIntro.cn: 该词族可追溯到拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的）。

items.example: He drank a saucerful of soup.
Heat the soup in a saucepan.

items.meaning: a disc-shaped object seen in the sky

definition_en: finely chopped meat packed into a thin casing
core_image: 平底锅里几根香肠滋滋作响，表皮变成金棕色
scene: 早餐时，平底锅里煎着几根香肠。Two sausages are frying in the pan.
sceneCN: 这里 sausage 是「香肠」（第 1 个义项）；句意：两根香肠正在锅里煎着。

senses.title: Meat in a casing
senses.definition: finely chopped meat packed into a thin casing
senses.definitionCN: 切碎后灌入细肠衣的肉
senses.example: They grilled sausages for lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他们午餐烤了香肠。
senses.why: The core sense is chopped meat shaped by a casing.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是用肠衣定型的碎肉。

senses.title: Processed sausage product
senses.definition: a manufactured meat product sold in a sausage shape
senses.definitionCN: 做成香肠形状出售的加工肉制品
senses.example: He bought a packet of sausage snacks.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一包香肠零食。
senses.why: The casing shape extends to industrial meat products.
senses.whyCN: 肠衣的形状扩展到工业肉制品。

senses.title: Sausage shape
senses.definition: something long and rounded like a sausage
senses.definitionCN: 像香肠一样细长而圆的东西
senses.example: The balloon was twisted into a sausage shape.
senses.exampleCN: 气球被扭成了香肠的形状。
senses.why: The food shape becomes a way to describe other objects.
senses.whyCN: 食物形状成为描述其他物体的方式。

intro.en: Sausage traces from Latin salsus through Late Latin salsicia and Old French.
intro.cn: sausage 经晚期拉丁语 salsicia 和古法语，追溯到拉丁语 salsus。

items.en: Salsus means salted.
items.cn: salsus 意为盐腌的。

items.en: Salsicia named salted meat preparations.
items.cn: salsicia 指盐腌的肉类食品。

items.en: Saussiche named a seasoned meat casing.
items.cn: saussiche 指调味肉肠。

items.en: Sausige appeared for minced meat in a skin.
items.cn: sausige 指灌在肠衣中的碎肉。

items.en: Sausage covers fresh, cured, and industrial products.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sausage 兼指鲜肠、腊肠和工业制品。

note.en: Sausage is compared with look-alike words and other meat products.
note.cn: 把 sausage 与形近词和其他肉制品作比较。

entries.definition: a small dish under a cup
a sausage served in a long bun

normalIntro.en: Sausage can be remembered by its salt root and its shape.
normalIntro.cn: 可以从盐腌词根和细长形状两方面记住 sausage。

normal.en: Sausage begins like sauce, because both come from salted food.
normal.cn: sausage 开头像 sauce，因为两者都源自盐腌食物。

normal.en: The long body of the word looks like a sausage link.
normal.cn: 这个单词长长的词形像一截香肠。

normal.en: Sausages are often fried, so picture them in a hot pan.
normal.cn: 香肠常被煎，想象它们在热锅里。

normal.en: A sausage roll wraps the meat in pastry.
normal.cn: 香肠卷把肉包在酥皮里。

normal.en: The plural sausages adds s and keeps the soft ge sound.
normal.cn: 复数 sausages 加 s，并保留柔和的 ge 音。

abstract.en: A casing turns scattered meat into one neat form.
abstract.cn: 肠衣把零散的肉变成一个整齐的整体。

abstract.en: Salt once preserved meat through long winters.
abstract.cn: 盐曾经帮助人们在漫长冬季保存肉类。

abstract.en: The sausage shape is simple enough to describe almost anything.
abstract.cn: 香肠的形状简单到几乎可以形容任何东西。

examples.en: She sliced the sausage for the pasta.
examples.cn: 她把香肠切片放进意面。

examples.en: The smell of fried sausage filled the kitchen.
examples.cn: 煎香肠的香味充满了厨房。

examples.en: He ate a sausage roll on the train.
examples.cn: 他在火车上吃了一个香肠卷。

dict_mnemonic.text: sausage 与 sauce 同源，都和盐腌有关，可记「用盐腌好、灌进肠衣的肉」。

root: 源自拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的），经晚期拉丁语 salsicia 与古法语 saussiche 进入英语，核心义「盐腌碎肉灌成的肠」。

sensesIntro.en: Sausage means chopped meat in a casing, a processed meat product, or a sausage shape.
sensesIntro.cn: sausage 意为灌在肠衣里的碎肉、加工肉制品，或香肠形状。

core.en: Salted chopped meat shaped inside a casing.
core.cn: 在肠衣中定型的盐腌碎肉。

branches.en: The core food, meat packed in a casing.
branches.cn: 核心食物，灌入肠衣的肉。

branches.en: Manufactured meat products in sausage form.
branches.cn: 做成香肠形状的加工肉制品。

branches.en: Any object with a long rounded shape.
branches.cn: 任何细长浑圆的物体。

branches.en: Both are meat sold in a casing or tube.
branches.cn: 两者都是肠衣或管状包装出售的肉。

branches.en: The industrial product keeps the food shape.
branches.cn: 工业制品保留了食物的形状。

intro.en: Sausage belongs to the salted-food family of sauce.
intro.cn: sausage 属于 sauce 的盐腌食物词族。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin salsus, salted.
latinIntro.cn: 其词根是拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的）。

items.example: Mix the sausage meat with herbs.
items.exampleCN: 把香肠肉馅和香草拌在一起。

items.example: His saucy joke made us laugh.
items.exampleCN: 他俏皮的笑话逗笑了我们。
萨尔萨辣酱配薯片很好。

latinEntries.example: Sal is the Latin word for salt.

definition_en: to keep safe from harm, to use less, or to put money aside
core_image: 救生员跃入泳池，把孩子托出水面
scene: 泳池边，救生员跳入水中救起孩子。The lifeguard saved the child from drowning.
sceneCN: 这里 save 是「挽救」（第 1 个义项）；句意：救生员把孩子从溺水中救了出来。

senses.title: Rescue from harm
senses.definition: to keep someone or something safe from danger or harm
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物免于危险或伤害
senses.example: The doctor saved the boy's life.
senses.exampleCN: 医生救了男孩的命。
senses.why: The oldest sense is bringing someone out of danger.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是把人从危险中带出来。

senses.title: Use less
senses.definition: to avoid wasting money, time, or resources
senses.definitionCN: 避免浪费金钱、时间或资源
senses.example: Taking the train saves time.
senses.exampleCN: 坐火车能节省时间。
senses.why: Rescuing a resource from waste becomes saving it.
senses.whyCN: 把资源从浪费中救出，就变成节省。

senses.title: Put money aside
senses.definition: to keep money for future use
senses.definitionCN: 把钱留作将来使用
senses.example: She saves a little every month.
senses.exampleCN: 她每月存一点钱。
senses.why: Money kept safe for later is money saved.
senses.whyCN: 为以后安全留存的钱就是储蓄。

senses.title: Store a file
senses.definition: to store work in a computer so it can be used later
senses.definitionCN: 把工作内容存入电脑以便以后使用
senses.example: Remember to save the document.
senses.exampleCN: 记得保存文档。
senses.why: Digital storage keeps work safe from loss.
senses.whyCN: 数字存储让工作成果免于丢失。

senses.title: Spare someone
senses.definition: to prevent someone from having to do something unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 使某人不必做不愉快的事
senses.example: I will save you the trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 我会省去你的麻烦。
senses.why: Spared effort is effort saved.
senses.whyCN: 省去的力气就是被节省的力气。

intro.en: Save comes from Latin salvare, to make safe, through Old French sauver.
intro.cn: save 经古法语 sauver，源自拉丁语 salvare（使安全）。

items.en: Salvare means to make safe or to rescue.
items.cn: salvare 意为使安全或拯救。

items.en: Salvus means safe and uninjured.
items.cn: salvus 意为安全无恙的。

items.en: Sauver carried the sense of rescuing and sparing.
items.cn: sauver 兼具拯救与省下之义。

items.en: Saven added the sense of keeping money.
items.cn: saven 增加了存钱的含义。

items.en: Save extends to time, files, and effort.
items.cn: 现代英语中 save 扩展到时间、文件和精力。

note.en: Save is compared with similar spellings and with words for rescuing or keeping.
note.cn: 把 save 与形近词以及表示拯救或保留的词作比较。

entries.definition: to keep something in good condition

normalIntro.en: Save can be remembered through its sense of keeping safe.
normalIntro.cn: 可以通过「保持安全」这一核心意思记住 save。

normal.en: Save and safe share the same opening sound and meaning.
normal.cn: save 与 safe 开头音相同，意思也相通。

normal.en: Saving money keeps it safe for another day.
normal.cn: 存钱就是把钱安全留到以后用。

normal.en: A lifeguard saves a swimmer, while a saver saves cash.
normal.cn: 救生员救人，储蓄者存钱，都是 save。

normal.en: Press save before closing the document.
normal.cn: 关闭文档前按下保存键。

normal.en: The past form saved is made by adding d.
normal.cn: 过去式 saved 只需在词尾加 d。

abstract.en: To save is to give something a second chance.
abstract.cn: 拯救就是给某物第二次机会。

abstract.en: Every saved minute is a minute returned to you.
abstract.cn: 每一分钟节省下来的时间都是还给你的时间。

abstract.en: Saving links the present self with the future self.
abstract.cn: 储蓄把现在的自己与未来的自己连接起来。

examples.en: The new system saves the company a lot of money.
examples.cn: 新系统为公司节省了大量资金。

examples.en: He saved enough to buy a small car.
examples.cn: 他攒够了钱买一辆小车。

examples.en: Please save your work before the computer restarts.
examples.cn: 电脑重启前请保存你的工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: save 与 safe（安全的）同源，核心是「使安全」：救人、省资源、存钱、存文件都是让东西不丢失。

root: 源自拉丁语 salvare（使安全），与 salvus（安全的）同源，核心义「使免于损失或危险」。

sensesIntro.en: Save means to rescue, to use less, to put money aside, to store a file, or to spare someone trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: save 意为拯救、节省、储蓄、保存文件，或省去某人的麻烦。

core.en: To keep someone or something safe from loss.
core.cn: 使某人或某物免于损失。

branches.en: The core act of rescuing from harm.
branches.cn: 从危险中救出的核心行为。

branches.en: Resources kept from being wasted.
branches.cn: 使资源免于浪费。

branches.en: Money kept safe for future needs.
branches.cn: 为将来需要而安全保留的钱。

branches.en: Computer work stored against loss.
branches.cn: 防止丢失而存储的电脑成果。

branches.en: Trouble removed from someone.
branches.cn: 为某人省去的麻烦。

intro.en: Save has a broad family built on the idea of safety.
intro.cn: save 有一个围绕「安全」概念扩展的大家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin salvare and salvus lie behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salvare 与 salvus 是这一英语词族的来源。

items.meaning: a person or thing that saves

items.example: The change gave us a saving of ten pounds.
items.exampleCN: 这一改动让我们省了十英镑。

items.example: Her savings are in the bank.

definition_en: to speak words, to express something, or to give a stated meaning
core_image: 会议上一个人举起手，准备说出自己的看法
scene: 会议上，他举手要求发言。He raised his hand to say something.
sceneCN: 这里 say 是「说」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他举手想说点什么。

senses.title: Speak words
senses.definition: to speak words in order to express something
senses.definitionCN: 说出话语以表达某事
senses.example: She said she would come later.
senses.exampleCN: 她说她会晚点来。
senses.why: The basic sense is producing speech.
senses.whyCN: 基本义是发出话语。

senses.title: Show in writing
senses.definition: of a sign or text, to show or state something
senses.definitionCN: 指标牌或文字显示、写明某事
senses.example: The notice says the shop is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 告示上写着商店关门。
senses.why: Written words speak to the reader.
senses.whyCN: 书面文字也在向读者说话。

senses.title: For example
senses.definition: used to introduce an example or an approximate amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出例子或大概的数量
senses.example: Take an apple, say, and cut it in half.
senses.exampleCN: 比如说拿一个苹果，把它切成两半。
senses.why: The speaker says a possible case aloud.
senses.whyCN: 说话者把一种可能情况说出来。

senses.title: Right to speak
senses.definition: the chance or right to express an opinion
senses.definitionCN: 表达意见的机会或权利
senses.example: Everyone should have a say in the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都应对这个计划有发言权。
senses.why: The act of saying becomes the right to be heard.
senses.whyCN: 说的行为转化为被倾听的权利。

intro.en: Say is a native English word from Old English secgan, with Germanic roots.
intro.cn: say 是英语本族词，源自古英语 secgan，属于日耳曼语源。

items.en: Sagjan meant to tell or to state.
items.cn: sagjan 意为讲述或陈述。

items.en: Secgan meant to say or to tell.
items.cn: secgan 意为说或告诉。

items.en: Seien simplified the spelling and kept the sound.
items.cn: seien 简化了拼写并保留读音。

items.en: Say became the standard form for speaking.
items.cn: say 成为表示说话的标准形式。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as needless to say grew common.
items.cn: needless to say 等固定短语逐渐常见。

note.en: Say is compared with look-alike spellings and with other speech verbs.
note.cn: 把 say 与形近拼写以及其他言说动词作比较。

entries.definition: to kill in a violent way

normalIntro.en: Say is short, common, and changes sharply in the past tense.
normalIntro.cn: say 简短常用，过去式变化不规则。

normal.en: Say is one syllable, like the quick act of speaking.
normal.cn: say 是一个音节，正像说话这个快速动作。

normal.en: The past form said rhymes with red.
normal.cn: 过去式 said 与 red 押韵。

normal.en: Say hello and say goodbye are two daily phrases.
normal.cn: say hello 和 say goodbye 是两个日常短语。

normal.en: A saying is a short sentence people often repeat.
normal.cn: saying 是人们常重复的短句。

normal.en: Have a say means having a voice in a decision.
normal.cn: have a say 意为在决定中有发言权。

abstract.en: To say is to turn a thought into sound.
abstract.cn: 说就是把想法变成声音。

abstract.en: A word said today may echo for years.
abstract.cn: 今天说出的一句话可能回响多年。

abstract.en: Saying and listening are two halves of one conversation.
abstract.cn: 说与听是同一场对话的两半。

examples.en: What did she say about the meeting?
examples.cn: 她关于会议说了什么？

examples.en: The sign says no parking.
examples.cn: 牌子上写着禁止停车。

examples.en: Everyone will have a say in the final choice.
examples.cn: 每个人在最终选择中都会有发言权。

dict_mnemonic.text: say 是英语本族词，记 its 不规则变化：say, says, said；再记短语 have a say（有发言权）。

root: 源自古英语 secgan（说、告诉），属日耳曼语源，核心义「用话语表达」。

sensesIntro.en: Say means to speak, to show in writing, to give an example, or to have a right to speak.
sensesIntro.cn: say 意为说话、书面表明、举例说明，或拥有发言权。

core.en: To express something in words.
core.cn: 用话语表达某事。

branches.en: The core act of speaking words.
branches.cn: 说出话语的核心行为。

branches.en: Words on a sign or page speaking to readers.
branches.cn: 标牌或纸面上的文字向读者传达信息。

branches.en: A possible case stated aloud as an example.
branches.cn: 作为例子说出的可能情况。

branches.en: The right to make one's voice heard.
branches.cn: 让自己的声音被听见的权利。

branches.en: Spoken and written words both convey meaning.
branches.cn: 口头与书面文字都传递意义。

intro.en: Say forms several common compounds and derivatives.
intro.cn: say 构成若干常见复合词和派生词。

latinIntro.en: Say is Germanic rather than Latin, so the Latin entries list related concepts only.
latinIntro.cn: say 属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁条目只列相关概念。

items.exampleCN: 这个想法几乎难以表达。

items.example: No one can gainsay the facts.

items.meaning: a person who predicts the future

items.example: Some things are better left unsaid.

definition_en: the size or extent of something, a set of marks for measuring, or a thin plate on a fish
core_image: 地图角落的一小段比例尺，标注着图上距离与现实距离的关系
scene: 地图下方标着比例尺。A scale is printed at the bottom of the map.
sceneCN: 这里 scale 是「刻度；比例尺」（第 2 个义项）；句意：地图底部印着比例尺。

senses.title: Size and extent
senses.definition: the size or extent of something, especially when large
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的规模或范围，尤指较大规模
senses.example: The project was built on a huge scale.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目以巨大的规模建成。
senses.why: The core abstract sense is how far something reaches.
senses.whyCN: 核心抽象义是事物所达到的范围。

senses.title: Measuring marks
senses.definition: a set of marks or numbers used for measuring
senses.definitionCN: 用于测量的一组刻度或数字
senses.example: Read the weight on the scale.
senses.exampleCN: 读出秤上的重量。
senses.why: A ladder of marks turns size into a readable measure.
senses.whyCN: 一串刻度把大小转化为可读的度量。

senses.title: Fish plate
senses.definition: one of the thin hard plates covering a fish or reptile
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖鱼或爬行动物身体的薄硬片
senses.example: The fish's scales shone in the light.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼鳞在光下闪闪发亮。
senses.why: The layered plates look like small measuring marks.
senses.whyCN: 层叠的薄片看起来像小刻度。

senses.title: Weighing device
senses.definition: a device with two pans for weighing, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 通常用复数形式，指带两个秤盘的天平
senses.example: Place the fruit on the scales.
senses.exampleCN: 把水果放在秤上。
senses.why: The balanced beam is marked like a measuring scale.
senses.whyCN: 平衡的横梁像测量刻度一样被标记。

senses.title: Climb up
senses.definition: to climb up or over something steep
senses.definitionCN: 攀上或翻越陡峭之物
senses.example: They scaled the wall before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在黎明前翻过了墙。
senses.why: Climbing a ladder resembles moving up a scale.
senses.whyCN: 爬梯子就像沿着刻度向上移动。

senses.title: Resize proportionally
senses.definition: to change the size of something while keeping its proportions
senses.definitionCN: 在保持比例的情况下改变某物的大小
senses.example: Scale the image to fit the page.
senses.exampleCN: 把图片缩放到适合页面。
senses.why: A scale keeps every part in the same ratio.
senses.whyCN: 比例尺让每个部分保持相同比率。

intro.en: Scale comes from Latin scala, a ladder or flight of steps.
intro.cn: scale 源自拉丁语 scala，意为梯子或一段台阶。

items.en: Scala means a ladder or a flight of steps.
items.cn: scala 意为梯子或一段台阶。

items.en: Scalae, the plural, named steps used for climbing.
items.cn: 复数 scalae 指用于攀爬的台阶。

items.en: Escale carried the sense of a ladder and a measure.
items.cn: escale 兼有梯子和度量之义。

items.en: Scale named a graduated measure and a climbing act.
items.cn: scale 指分级刻度和攀登动作。

items.en: The musical scale borrowed the ladder image.
items.cn: 音乐音阶借用了梯子的意象。

items.en: Scale extends to maps, models, and business size.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scale 扩展到地图、模型和商业规模。

note.en: Scale is compared with similar spellings and with words for size and measurement.
note.cn: 把 scale 与形近词以及表示大小和度量的词作比较。

entries.definition: the skin on the top of the head
a shellfish with a fan-shaped shell
the area or degree something covers
the limits between which something varies
a relationship between sizes or amounts

normalIntro.en: Scale can be remembered as a ladder of marks that measures many things.
normalIntro.cn: 可以把 scale 记成一串刻度阶梯，用来度量许多事物。

normal.en: A scale is a ladder of marks, from Latin scala.
normal.cn: scale 是一串刻度阶梯，源自拉丁语 scala。

normal.en: Fish scales overlap like the steps of a tiny ladder.
normal.cn: 鱼鳞层叠，就像微型梯子的台阶。

normal.en: Scale up means enlarge, scale down means reduce.
normal.cn: scale up 是扩大，scale down 是缩小。

normal.en: On a large scale means at a great size.
normal.cn: on a large scale 意为以巨大规模。

normal.en: The scales in a bathroom measure your weight.
normal.cn: 浴室的秤用来测量体重。

abstract.en: Every scale is a promise that size can be compared.
abstract.cn: 每一种刻度都意味着大小可以被比较。

abstract.en: A model keeps the scale but loses the weight.
abstract.cn: 模型保留比例，却失去了重量。

abstract.en: Climbing and measuring share the image of steps.
abstract.cn: 攀登与测量共享台阶的意象。

examples.en: The company expanded on an international scale.
examples.cn: 这家公司以国际规模扩张。

examples.en: The map has a scale of one to fifty thousand.
examples.cn: 这张地图的比例尺是一比五万。

examples.en: Workers scaled the cliff to reach the cave.
examples.cn: 工人们攀上悬崖到达洞穴。

dict_mnemonic.text: scale 源自「梯子」，梯子的台阶就是刻度；由此引申出规模、比例尺、音阶、鱼鳞和攀登。

root: 源自拉丁语 scala（梯子、台阶），核心义「一级一级的量度」，由此扩展到规模、刻度、比例与攀登。

sensesIntro.en: Scale means size, measuring marks, fish plates, a weighing device, climbing, or resizing.
sensesIntro.cn: scale 意为规模、刻度、鱼鳞、天平、攀登，或按比例缩放。

core.en: A ladder-like set of steps used to measure or climb.
core.cn: 像梯子一样用于度量或攀爬的一级级台阶。

branches.en: Measured size becomes the idea of scale.
branches.cn: 被度量的大小成为规模概念。

branches.en: The marks themselves form a measuring scale.
branches.cn: 刻度本身构成测量标尺。

branches.en: Overlapping plates resemble tiny steps.
branches.cn: 层叠的鳞片像微小的台阶。

branches.en: The weighing beam is marked like a scale.
branches.cn: 天平横梁像刻度尺一样被标记。

branches.en: Climbing up and scaling an image both follow a ratio.
branches.cn: 向上攀登与缩放图像都遵循某种比率。

intro.en: Scale has a productive family in measurement and technology.
intro.cn: scale 在度量与技术领域有能产的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scala, a ladder, is the source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scala（梯子）是整个词族的来源。

items.meaning: a weighing device or fish plates
the act of climbing or resizing
items.example: Scaling the wall took an hour.

items.meaning: able to grow or be resized

items.example: They tested the scalability of the app.
items.exampleCN: 他们测试了应用的可扩展性。

items.meaning: a device or program that resizes

items.example: They plan to scale up production.
We must scale down the design.
items.exampleCN: 我们必须缩小设计规模。

definition_en: to pass a device over something, to look through quickly, or to examine closely
core_image: 一束光在纸面上来回移动，把文字变成电脑里的图像
scene: 医生把片子放进机器里扫描。The doctor scanned the image for problems.
sceneCN: 这里 scan 是「扫描」（第 1 个义项）；句意：医生扫描图像查找问题。

senses.title: Use a scanning device
senses.definition: to pass a machine or beam over something to read or record it
senses.definitionCN: 让机器或光束掠过某物以读取或记录
senses.example: Please scan the barcode at the till.
senses.exampleCN: 请在收银台扫描条形码。
senses.why: The core sense is a moving beam that captures a surface.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是移动的光束捕捉一个表面。

senses.title: Look through quickly
senses.definition: to read or look through something quickly
senses.definitionCN: 快速阅读或查看某物
senses.example: I scanned the menu and chose soup.
senses.exampleCN: 我浏览菜单，选了汤。
senses.why: The eye sweeps the page like a scanning beam.
senses.whyCN: 目光像扫描光束一样掠过页面。

senses.title: Examine closely
senses.definition: to examine something carefully in search of details
senses.definitionCN: 仔细检查某物以寻找细节
senses.example: He scanned her face for a sign.
senses.exampleCN: 他审视她的脸寻找迹象。
senses.why: A slow scan searches every part of the surface.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢扫描会探查表面的每个部分。

senses.title: Mark verse metre
senses.definition: to mark the stressed and unstressed beats of a poem
senses.definitionCN: 标出诗句中的重读与非重读音步
senses.example: Students scanned the lines of Latin verse.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们标出拉丁诗句的格律。
senses.why: The old sense is climbing through a line beat by beat.
senses.whyCN: 古老义项是逐拍走过一行诗。

senses.title: Medical image
senses.definition: a medical test that produces an image of the inside of the body
senses.definitionCN: 生成身体内部图像的医学检查
senses.example: The scan showed a small fracture.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示有一处小骨折。
senses.why: The device action becomes the name of the test.
senses.whyCN: 设备动作转化为检查的名称。

intro.en: Scan comes from Latin scandere, to climb, which also meant to scan verse.
intro.cn: scan 源自拉丁语 scandere（攀登），也指逐拍分析诗句。

items.en: Scandere means to climb or mount.
items.cn: scandere 意为攀登、上升。

items.en: Scansion named the marking of verse rhythm.
items.cn: scansion 指标记诗句节奏。

items.en: Scanning verse meant moving through each foot.
items.cn: 分析诗句意味着逐个音步走过。

items.en: Scanen meant to examine verse closely.
items.cn: scanen 意为仔细分析诗句。

items.en: The word extended to beams and medical imaging.
items.cn: 该词扩展到光束与医学成像。

note.en: Scan is compared with similar spellings and with other ways of looking.
note.cn: 把 scan 与形近词以及其它观看方式作比较。

entries.definition: a mark left by a wound
to read quickly for the main idea
to move quickly over an area

normalIntro.en: Scan joins the idea of climbing through verse with sweeping a beam over a surface.
normalIntro.cn: scan 把逐拍走过诗句与光束扫过表面联系起来。

normal.en: A scanner sweeps a line of light across the page.
normal.cn: 扫描仪让一条光扫过页面。

normal.en: To scan a menu is to sweep your eyes down it fast.
normal.cn: scan 菜单就是目光快速向下扫过。

normal.en: The double n appears in scanned and scanning.
normal.cn: scanned 和 scanning 中都有双写 n。

normal.en: A brain scan is a picture made by scanning.
normal.cn: 脑部扫描是由扫描生成的图像。

normal.en: Scan the crowd means searching faces quickly.
normal.cn: scan the crowd 意为快速搜寻人脸。

abstract.en: Scanning turns a surface into information.
abstract.cn: 扫描把一个表面转化为信息。

abstract.en: Fast looking finds the shape; slow scanning finds the detail.
abstract.cn: 快速浏览找到轮廓，缓慢扫描找到细节。

abstract.en: The beam and the eye both move in lines.
abstract.cn: 光束和目光都以线条移动。

examples.en: She scanned the receipt into the computer.
examples.cn: 她把收据扫描进电脑。

examples.en: He scanned the report for any mention of cost.
examples.cn: 他快速浏览报告寻找有关成本的提及。

examples.en: The guard scanned the crowd at the gate.
examples.cn: 警卫在门口扫视人群。

dict_mnemonic.text: scan 原指「一步步攀登」诗句的格律，后来引申为光束一行行扫过，即扫描；再引申为目光快速浏览。

root: 源自拉丁语 scandere（攀登），经「逐拍分析诗行」引申为扫视、扫描，核心义「一行行地掠过」。

sensesIntro.en: Scan means to use a beam or machine, to look through quickly, to examine closely, or a medical image.
sensesIntro.cn: scan 意为用光束或机器扫描、快速浏览、仔细审视，或医学扫描检查。

core.en: To move steadily across a surface, as a beam or an eye.
core.cn: 像光束或目光一样稳定地掠过表面。

branches.en: A device sweeps and records a surface.
branches.cn: 设备掠过并记录表面。

branches.en: The eye sweeps text for key points.
branches.cn: 目光掠过文字抓取要点。

branches.en: The eye moves slowly to catch details.
branches.cn: 目光缓慢移动以捕捉细节。

branches.en: The old sense of walking through verse beats.
branches.cn: 逐拍走过诗句的古老义项。

branches.en: The action of scanning produces a medical scan.
branches.cn: 扫描动作产生了医学扫描检查。

intro.en: Scan has a small but active family in technology and poetry.
intro.cn: scan 在技术与诗歌领域有一个小而活跃的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb scandere, to climb, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 scandere（攀登）是远源。

items.meaning: to sweep over or a medical test

latinEntries.meaning: a climbing or scanning of verse

definition_en: an action or event that causes public shock and disapproval
core_image: 报纸头版印着醒目的标题，路人停下脚步议论纷纷
scene: 报纸头版爆出公司财务丑闻。The newspaper revealed a financial scandal.
sceneCN: 这里 scandal 是「丑闻」（第 1 个义项）；句意：报纸揭露了一起财务丑闻。

senses.title: Public disgrace
senses.definition: an action or event that causes public shock and disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 引起公众震惊与谴责的行为或事件
senses.example: The minister resigned over a corruption scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 部长因腐败丑闻辞职。
senses.why: The core sense is a public shock that damages reputation.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是损害名誉的公共震惊事件。

senses.title: Malicious gossip
senses.definition: talk that spreads shocking or unkind stories about people
senses.definitionCN: 传播关于他人的惊人或不友善故事的闲话
senses.example: The village was full of scandal about the new neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 村里到处都是关于新邻居的流言。
senses.why: The shock of an event feeds the talk that spreads it.
senses.whyCN: 事件的震惊滋养了传播它的闲话。

senses.title: Moral outrage
senses.definition: a feeling of shock and moral disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 震惊与道德上的不赞同之感
senses.example: Their behaviour caused scandal among the older guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的行为在年长宾客中引起反感。
senses.why: The event produces the emotion it is named for.
senses.whyCN: 事件产生了以之命名的情绪。

intro.en: Scandal comes from Greek skandalon, a trap or stumbling block, through Latin.
intro.cn: scandal 经拉丁语源自希腊语 skandalon，意为陷阱或绊脚石。

items.en: Skandalon means a snare or a cause of stumbling.
items.cn: skandalon 意为圈套或使人跌倒的原因。

items.en: Scandalum meant a stumbling block or offence.
items.cn: scandalum 意为绊脚石或冒犯。

items.en: Scandale carried the sense of public disgrace.
items.cn: scandale 带有公开耻辱之义。

items.en: Scandal named shameful conduct and gossip.
items.cn: scandal 指可耻行为与流言。

items.en: Scandal covers politics, business, and celebrity life.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scandal 涵盖政治、商业与名人生活。

note.en: Scandal is compared with similar spellings and with words for shame and gossip.
note.cn: 把 scandal 与形近词以及表示耻辱和流言的词作比较。

entries.definition: a strong feeling of shock and anger
talk about other people's private lives

normalIntro.en: Scandal can be remembered through its sense of a public stumble.
normalIntro.cn: 可以通过「当众跌倒」的意思记住 scandal。

normal.en: A scandal is a public stumble that everyone sees.
normal.cn: 丑闻是所有人都看见的当众失足。

normal.en: The word has scan at the beginning and dal at the end.
normal.cn: 这个词开头是 scan，结尾是 dal。

normal.en: A corruption scandal often ends a career.
normal.cn: 腐败丑闻常常终结一个人的职业生涯。

normal.en: Scandalous describes behaviour that shocks people.
normal.cn: scandalous 形容令人震惊的行为。

normal.en: A scandal sheet is a paper full of gossip.
normal.cn: scandal sheet 是充满八卦的小报。

abstract.en: A scandal is a private failure made public.
abstract.cn: 丑闻是被公开的私人失败。

abstract.en: Gossip spreads a scandal faster than facts can.
abstract.cn: 流言传播丑闻比事实更快。

abstract.en: The word once meant a trap, and a scandal still catches people.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指陷阱，而丑闻至今仍会让人中招。

examples.en: The scandal damaged the company's reputation.
examples.cn: 这起丑闻损害了公司的声誉。

examples.en: Reporters kept the scandal alive for weeks.
examples.cn: 记者们让这桩丑闻持续发酵了数周。

examples.en: She refused to take part in the gossip and scandal.
examples.cn: 她拒绝参与那些流言蜚语。

dict_mnemonic.text: scandal 原指「绊倒人的陷阱」，一个人当众跌倒就成丑闻；可记「当众失足，满城风雨」。

root: 源自希腊语 skandalon（陷阱、绊脚石），经拉丁语 scandalum 入英语，核心义「使人跌倒、招致公愤的事」。

sensesIntro.en: Scandal means a shocking public event, the gossip around it, or the outrage it causes.
sensesIntro.cn: scandal 意为令人震惊的公开事件、围绕它的流言，或它引起的愤慨。

core.en: A public shock caused by shameful behaviour.
core.cn: 可耻行为引起的公众震惊。

branches.en: The core event that shocks the public.
branches.cn: 震惊公众的核心事件。

branches.en: Talk that spreads the shocking story.
branches.cn: 传播惊人故事的闲话。

branches.en: The moral outrage felt by observers.
branches.cn: 旁观者感到的道德愤慨。

branches.en: An event and the gossip about it feed each other.
branches.cn: 事件与关于它的流言相互助长。

branches.en: A shameful event produces public outrage.
branches.cn: 可耻事件引发公众愤慨。

intro.en: Scandal has a family of adjectives, verbs, and compounds.
intro.cn: scandal 有形容词、动词和复合词构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scandalum, a stumbling block, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scandalum（绊脚石）是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 这番话让观众大为震惊。
散布丑闻的人毁了她的名声。

items.example: He never reads a scandal sheet.

items.exampleCN: 受丑闻打击的银行失去了客户。

definition_en: a mark left on skin or feelings after a wound has healed
core_image: 手臂上一道淡白色的旧疤，记录着多年前的一次事故
scene: 事故多年后，他胳膊上仍有一道疤。A scar remains on his arm.
sceneCN: 这里 scar 是「伤疤」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的胳膊上留着一道疤。

senses.title: Mark on skin
senses.definition: a mark left on the skin after a wound has healed
senses.definitionCN: 伤口愈合后留在皮肤上的痕迹
senses.example: The cut left a small scar on her knee.
senses.exampleCN: 那道割伤在她膝盖上留下了一个小疤。
senses.why: The core sense is the visible trace of healing.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是愈合留下的可见痕迹。

senses.title: Emotional wound
senses.definition: a lasting emotional hurt caused by a bad experience
senses.definitionCN: 糟糕经历造成的持久情感伤害
senses.example: The loss left deep scars on the family.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失去给这个家庭留下了深深的创伤。
senses.why: A mark on the mind mirrors a mark on the skin.
senses.whyCN: 心灵上的印记与皮肤上的印记相呼应。

senses.title: Leave a mark
senses.definition: to mark or damage someone or something permanently
senses.definitionCN: 永久地在某人或某物上留下痕迹或伤害
senses.example: The accident scarred him for life.
senses.exampleCN: 那场事故给他留下了终生的创伤。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb for causing the mark.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示造成痕迹的动词。

intro.en: Scar comes through Old French from Latin eschara, a scab, and Greek eskhara.
intro.cn: scar 经古法语源自拉丁语 eschara（痂），更早来自希腊语 eskhara。

items.en: Eskhara meant a hearth or a scab.
items.cn: eskhara 意为炉灶或痂。

items.en: Eschara meant a scab or scar.
items.cn: eschara 意为痂或疤痕。

items.en: Escarre named a mark left by a wound.
items.cn: escarre 指伤口留下的痕迹。

items.en: Scarre entered English with the same meaning.
items.cn: scarre 以相同含义进入英语。

items.en: Scar extends from skin to emotions and landscapes.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scar 从皮肤扩展到情感与地貌。

note.en: Scar is compared with similar spellings and with words for wounds and marks.
note.cn: 把 scar 与形近词以及表示伤口和痕迹的词作比较。

entries.definition: a cloth worn around the neck
a small visible spot or line
a small mark that spoils appearance

normalIntro.en: Scar is a short word for a long-lasting mark.
normalIntro.cn: scar 是一个表示持久痕迹的短词。

normal.en: A scar is what a wound leaves behind.
normal.cn: 伤疤是伤口留下的东西。

normal.en: Scar and scare differ by one letter.
normal.cn: scar 与 scare 只差一个字母。

normal.en: The double r appears in scarred and scarring.
normal.cn: scarred 和 scarring 中都有双写 r。

normal.en: Scar tissue is the body's repair material.
normal.cn: 疤痕组织是身体的修复材料。

normal.en: Emotional scars are invisible but real.
normal.cn: 情感创伤看不见却是真实存在的。

abstract.en: A scar is proof that healing happened.
abstract.cn: 伤疤是愈合发生过的证明。

abstract.en: Some marks fade, while others become part of us.
abstract.cn: 有些痕迹会淡去，有些则成为我们的一部分。

abstract.en: The same word covers skin and memory.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指皮肤也指记忆。

examples.en: The burn left a scar on his hand.
examples.cn: 烧伤在他手上留下了疤。

examples.en: Time can heal, but some scars remain.
examples.cn: 时间能治愈，但有些创伤仍在。

examples.en: The experience scarred her more than she admitted.
examples.cn: 这段经历给她的创伤比她承认的更深。

dict_mnemonic.text: scar 与 scare 形近；把「被吓到（scare）」和「留下疤（scar）」一起记：伤口会留下痕迹。

root: 经古法语 escarre 源自拉丁语 eschara（痂），更早为希腊语 eskhara，核心义「伤口愈合后留下的痕迹」。

sensesIntro.en: Scar means a mark on the skin, a lasting emotional hurt, or to leave such a mark.
sensesIntro.cn: scar 意为皮肤上的疤痕、持久的情感创伤，或留下这种痕迹。

core.en: A lasting mark left after healing.
core.cn: 愈合后留下的持久痕迹。

branches.en: The visible mark left on the skin.
branches.cn: 留在皮肤上的可见痕迹。

branches.en: An invisible mark left on feelings.
branches.cn: 留在情感上的无形痕迹。

branches.en: The act of leaving such a mark.
branches.cn: 留下这种痕迹的动作。

branches.en: Skin and mind both keep traces of injury.
branches.cn: 皮肤与心灵都会保留伤害的痕迹。

branches.en: A wound scars the body it damages.
branches.cn: 伤口会伤害并标记它所破坏的身体。

intro.en: Scar forms adjectives and nouns around healing and damage.
intro.cn: scar 围绕愈合与损伤构成形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin eschara and Greek eskhara, a scab, lie behind scar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 eschara 与希腊语 eskhara（痂）是 scar 的来源。

items.meaning: a mark or to leave one

items.exampleCN: 疤痕形成可能是永久的。

items.example: Scar tissue replaced the damaged skin.
items.exampleCN: 疤痕组织替代了受损的皮肤。
这个孩子背负着情感创伤。

definition_en: not available in large enough amounts; difficult to find
core_image: 干旱的土地上，水桶里只剩下浅浅一层水
scene: 旱季里，干净的水变得稀缺。Clean water is scarce during the dry season.
sceneCN: 这里 scarce 是「稀缺的；不足的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：旱季里干净的水很稀缺。

senses.title: Not enough in amount
senses.definition: existing in amounts too small for what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 数量太少，不足以满足需要
senses.example: Food was scarce after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后食物短缺。
senses.why: The core sense is a short supply of something needed.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是所需之物供应不足。

senses.title: Rare to find
senses.definition: uncommon and hard to find
senses.definitionCN: 不常见且难以找到
senses.example: Such birds are scarce in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟在这一带很罕见。
senses.why: A limited supply makes a thing uncommon.
senses.whyCN: 有限的供应使某物变得少见。

senses.title: In short supply
senses.definition: difficult to obtain because demand is higher than supply
senses.definitionCN: 因需求高于供应而难以获得
senses.example: Housing is scarce in the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 市中心住房供不应求。
senses.why: Economic shortage is the social form of scarcity.
senses.whyCN: 经济短缺是稀缺的社会形态。

intro.en: Scarce comes from Old French scars, from Latin excarpsus, plucked out.
intro.cn: scarce 源自法语古语 scars，更早来自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘除的）。

items.en: Excarpsus means plucked out or selected.
items.cn: excarpsus 意为被摘除或被挑出的。

items.en: Excerpere means to pick out or to take away.
items.cn: excerpere 意为挑出或拿走。

items.en: Scars meant sparing, limited, or hard to get.
items.cn: scars 意为节省的、有限的、难得的。

items.en: Scarce named a short supply of goods.
items.cn: scarce 指货物供应不足。

items.en: Scarce is central to economics and ecology.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scarce 是经济学与生态学的核心词。

note.en: Scarce is compared with similar spellings and with words for shortage.
note.cn: 把 scarce 与形近词以及表示短缺的词作比较。

entries.definition: a cloth worn around the neck
a mark left by a wound

normalIntro.en: Scarce and scarcity share a picture of empty shelves.
normalIntro.cn: scarce 与 scarcity 共享空货架的画面。

normal.en: A scarce item is like a shelf almost empty.
normal.cn: 稀缺的东西就像几乎空了的货架。

normal.en: Scarce adds ce to scar, but the sound is different.
normal.cn: scarce 比 scar 多了 ce，但读音不同。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun from scarce.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词形式。

normal.en: Scarce resources are a basic idea in economics.
normal.cn: 稀缺资源是经济学的基本概念。

normal.en: Clean water becomes scarce in a dry season.
normal.cn: 旱季里干净的水会变得稀缺。

abstract.en: Scarcity forces people to choose.
abstract.cn: 稀缺迫使人们做出选择。

abstract.en: What is scarce often becomes precious.
abstract.cn: 稀缺之物常常变得珍贵。

abstract.en: A full world still has scarce clean air.
abstract.cn: 即使世界很满，干净空气仍然稀缺。

examples.en: Jobs are scarce in the small town.
examples.cn: 这个小镇的工作机会很少。

examples.en: Water grew scarce as the summer went on.
examples.cn: 随着夏天推移，水变得稀缺。

examples.en: The government must decide how to share scarce resources.
examples.cn: 政府必须决定如何分配稀缺资源。

dict_mnemonic.text: scarce 与 scarcity 同族，可联想「空空的货架」：需要的东西不够，就是 scarce。

root: 源自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘出的），经古法语 scars 进入英语，核心义「被取走大半、所剩无几」。

sensesIntro.en: Scarce means not enough, hard to find, or in short supply.
sensesIntro.cn: scarce 意为数量不足、难以找到，或供不应求。

core.en: A supply that is too small for the need.
core.cn: 相对于需求而言过于稀少的供应。

branches.en: The core state of not having enough.
branches.cn: 数量不足的核心状态。

branches.en: Rarity makes a thing hard to find.
branches.cn: 稀有使某物难以找到。

branches.en: Demand outruns supply in the market.
branches.cn: 市场中需求超过供应。

branches.en: Too little of something makes it uncommon.
branches.cn: 某物太少就会变得不常见。

branches.en: Rarity and high demand create shortage.
branches.cn: 稀有与高需求共同造成短缺。

intro.en: Scarce forms nouns and adverbs about shortage.
intro.cn: scarce 构成表示短缺的名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin excerpere, to pick out, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excerpere（挑出）是远源。

items.example: The scarceness of rain worried farmers.
Clean water is the scarcest resource.
items.exampleCN: 干净的水是最稀缺的资源。
我们必须保护稀缺资源。

definition_en: only just; almost not at all
core_image: 赛跑终点线上，选手累得几乎站不住脚
scene: 他跑完比赛，累得几乎站不住。He could scarcely stand after the race.
sceneCN: 这里 scarcely 是「几乎不」（第 1 个义项）；句意：比赛结束后他几乎站不住。

senses.title: Almost not
senses.definition: only just; almost not at all
senses.definitionCN: 仅仅勉强；几乎完全不
senses.example: I could scarcely hear her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 我几乎听不见她的声音。
senses.why: The core sense is a very small degree, close to zero.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是程度极小，接近于零。

senses.title: Only just now
senses.definition: only a very short time before, often with when
senses.definitionCN: 就在很短时间之前，常与 when 连用
senses.example: We had scarcely sat down when the phone rang.
senses.exampleCN: 我们刚坐下电话就响了。
senses.why: A very small amount of time becomes just now.
senses.whyCN: 极少的时间量引申为「刚刚」。

senses.title: Certainly not
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is not true or possible
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调某事不真实或不可能
senses.example: This is scarcely the moment for jokes.
senses.exampleCN: 这可不是开玩笑的时候。
senses.why: Almost not becomes a strong denial in emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 「几乎没有」在强调中变成强烈的否定。

intro.en: Scarcely is scarce plus -ly, from Latin excarpsus, plucked out.
intro.cn: scarcely 由 scarce 加 -ly 构成，scarce 源自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘出的）。

items.en: Excarpsus means plucked out.
items.cn: excarpsus 意为被摘出的。

items.en: Scars meant sparing or limited.
items.cn: scars 意为节省的、有限的。

items.en: Scarce described a short supply.
items.cn: scarce 描述供应不足。

items.en: Scarcely added the adverb ending to scarce.
items.cn: scarcely 由 scarce 加副词词尾构成。

items.en: Scarcely is common in formal and literary sentences.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scarcely 常见于正式和文学语句。

note.en: Scarcely is compared with similar forms and with other negative adverbs.
note.cn: 把 scarcely 与形近形式以及其他否定副词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Scarcely is scarce with -ly, meaning almost not.
normalIntro.cn: scarcely 是 scarce 加 -ly，意为几乎不。

normal.en: Scarcely adds ly to scarce, just as safely adds ly to safe.
normal.cn: scarcely 像 safely 一样，在形容词后加 ly。

normal.en: Scarcely believe means you can almost not believe it.
normal.cn: scarcely believe 意为几乎不敢相信。

normal.en: Scarcely when means one thing follows another at once.
normal.cn: scarcely when 表示一事紧接着另一事发生。

normal.en: Hardly and scarcely are close synonyms.
normal.cn: hardly 与 scarcely 是近义词。

normal.en: The word is common in formal writing.
normal.cn: 这个词常见于正式写作。

abstract.en: Scarcely is the shadow of a yes that almost became a no.
abstract.cn: scarcely 是几乎变成否定的那一点肯定。

abstract.en: A scarce supply leaves scarcely any choice.
abstract.cn: 稀缺的供应让人几乎没有选择。

abstract.en: The adverb measures the distance between something and nothing.
abstract.cn: 这个副词衡量有与无之间的距离。

examples.en: She scarcely had time to eat.
examples.cn: 她几乎没有时间吃饭。

examples.en: Scarcely had he left when it began to rain.
examples.cn: 他刚离开就开始下雨了。

examples.en: I can scarcely believe the news.
examples.cn: 我几乎不敢相信这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: scarce 是「稀缺的」，加 -ly 成副词 scarcely，程度少到「几乎没有」。

root: 由 scarce 加 -ly 构成，scarce 源自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘出的），核心义「少到几乎不存在」。

sensesIntro.en: Scarcely means almost not, only just, or certainly not.
sensesIntro.cn: scarcely 意为几乎不、刚刚才，或决不。

core.en: A degree so small that it is almost nothing.
core.cn: 小到几乎等于零的程度。

branches.en: The core sense of almost not at all.
branches.cn: 几乎完全不的核心义。

branches.en: A tiny amount of time becomes just now.
branches.cn: 极少的时间量变成「刚刚」。

branches.en: Emphasis turns almost not into certainly not.
branches.cn: 强调把「几乎没有」变成「决不」。

branches.en: Barely enough and only just share the same limit.
branches.cn: 勉强够与刚刚才共享同一限度。

branches.en: Almost nothing can deny something outright.
branches.cn: 几乎没有可以变为断然否定。

intro.en: Scarcely belongs to the scarce family of shortage words.
intro.cn: scarcely 属于 scarce 的短缺词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin excerpere, to pick out, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excerpere（挑出）是远源。

items.example: The scarceness of food was serious.
items.exampleCN: 食物稀少的情况很严重。

definition_en: to make someone feel afraid, or to become afraid
core_image: 半夜一声怪响，孩子们猛地缩进被子里
scene: 半夜的怪声把孩子们吓坏了。A strange noise scared the children at midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 scare 是「惊吓」（第 1 个义项）；句意：半夜的怪声吓坏了孩子们。

senses.title: Frighten someone
senses.definition: to make a person or animal feel afraid
senses.definitionCN: 使人或动物感到害怕
senses.example: The loud bang scared the dog.
senses.exampleCN: 巨响吓到了狗。
senses.why: The core sense is causing sudden fear.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是引起突然的恐惧。

senses.title: Become frightened
senses.definition: to become afraid, especially of a sudden danger
senses.definitionCN: 尤指面对突然危险时变得害怕
senses.example: The horse scares easily at loud sounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹马容易被大声响吓到。
senses.why: The same action can be felt from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一动作也可以从受惊者内部来感受。

senses.title: Sudden alarm
senses.definition: a sudden feeling or period of public fear
senses.definitionCN: 突然的恐惧感或公众恐慌期
senses.example: The food scare led to empty shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 食品恐慌导致货架空荡。
senses.why: The verb becomes the name of the fear it creates.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为它所造成的恐惧的名称。

intro.en: Scare comes from Old Norse skjarr, timid, and entered English in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: scare 源自古诺尔斯语 skjarr（胆怯的），于中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Skjarr meant timid or easily frightened.
items.cn: skjarr 意为胆怯的、易受惊的。

items.en: Skerren meant to frighten or drive away.
items.cn: skerren 意为使害怕或驱赶。

items.en: Scare became the common verb for sudden fear.
items.cn: scare 成为表示突然恐惧的常用动词。

items.en: Scarecrow and scare tactics entered common use.
items.cn: scarecrow 与 scare tactics 进入常用语。

items.en: Scare also names public alarms such as health scares.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scare 也指健康恐慌等公众警报。

note.en: Scare is compared with similar spellings and with other fear verbs.
note.cn: 把 scare 与形近词以及其它表示恐惧的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a mark left by a wound
a cloth worn around the neck
to make someone worried or afraid

normalIntro.en: Scare is one letter away from scar, and both come from harm.
normalIntro.cn: scare 与 scar 只差一个字母，都与伤害有关。

normal.en: A scare can leave a scar on the memory.
normal.cn: 一次惊吓可能在记忆里留下疤痕。

normal.en: Scared is the adjective for feeling fear.
normal.cn: scared 是表示感到害怕的形容词。

normal.en: A scarecrow scares birds away from crops.
normal.cn: 稻草人把鸟从庄稼旁吓走。

normal.en: Scare away and scare off both mean drive off.
normal.cn: scare away 与 scare off 都表示吓退。

normal.en: A health scare is a sudden public worry about illness.
normal.cn: health scare 是关于疾病的突然公众担忧。

abstract.en: Fear arrives in a second but can last for years.
abstract.cn: 恐惧一秒钟到来，却可能持续多年。

abstract.en: A scare tests whether we can still think clearly.
abstract.cn: 惊吓检验我们是否还能清醒思考。

abstract.en: The same word names the act and the alarm.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指吓人的动作，也指惊慌。

examples.en: Don't scare me like that again.
examples.cn: 别再那样吓我了。

examples.en: The dog scared the birds out of the garden.
examples.cn: 狗把鸟吓出了花园。

examples.en: The city recovered after the food scare.
examples.cn: 食品恐慌过后，城市恢复了平静。

dict_mnemonic.text: scare 与 scar 形近，可记「被吓（scare）得留下疤（scar）」，核心是突然使人害怕。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 skjarr（胆怯的），经中古英语 skerren 进入英语，核心义「使人突然害怕」。

sensesIntro.en: Scare means to frighten someone, to become frightened, or a sudden alarm.
sensesIntro.cn: scare 意为吓唬某人、受惊害怕，或突然的恐慌。

core.en: Sudden fear caused by a threat.
core.cn: 由威胁引起的突然恐惧。

branches.en: Causing fear in another person or animal.
branches.cn: 使他人或动物产生恐惧。

branches.en: Being startled and feeling afraid.
branches.cn: 受到惊吓并感到害怕。

branches.en: A period of fear shared by many people.
branches.cn: 许多人共同经历的恐慌期。

branches.en: The giver and receiver of fear share one verb.
branches.cn: 施加恐惧者与承受恐惧者共用一个动词。

branches.en: A threat can scare one person or a whole city.
branches.cn: 一个威胁可以吓到一个人或整座城市。

intro.en: Scare builds a family of adjectives, tools, and tactics.
intro.cn: scare 构成形容词、工具和策略等词族。

latinIntro.en: Scare is Germanic, from Old Norse, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: scare 源自日耳曼语族中的古诺尔斯语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to frighten or a sudden alarm

items.example: She was scared of the dark.

items.meaning: a person or thing that scares
items.example: The machine is a bird scarer.

items.meaning: a figure set up to frighten birds
items.example: A scarecrow stood in the field.

items.exampleCN: 这场运动使用了恐吓手段。

definition_zh: 可怕的；胆小的；易受惊的
definition_en: making someone feel afraid, or easily frightened
core_image: 黑暗的走廊尽头，旧木门吱呀一声缓缓打开
scene: 黑暗中，旧楼梯发出吓人的响声。The old stairs made a scary noise in the dark.
sceneCN: 这里 scary 是「吓人的；可怕的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：黑暗中旧楼梯发出吓人的响声。

pos.zh: 令人不安的；毛骨悚然的

senses.title: Frightening
senses.definition: making someone feel fear
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到害怕的
senses.example: The roller coaster was scary but fun.
senses.exampleCN: 过山车很吓人但很好玩。
senses.why: The core sense is causing fear.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是引起恐惧。

senses.title: Easily frightened
senses.definition: easily frightened, used mainly in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 容易受惊的，主要用于非正式口语
senses.example: The scary little dog barked at everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 那只胆小的狗对谁都叫。
senses.why: The same ending can describe the one who feels fear.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词尾也可描述感到恐惧的一方。

senses.title: Eerie and unsettling
senses.titleCN: 令人不安的；毛骨悚然的
senses.definition: creating an uneasy feeling of threat or strangeness
senses.definitionCN: 造成威胁或怪异的不安感
senses.example: A scary silence filled the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 空房子里弥漫着令人不安的寂静。
senses.why: Fear can come from atmosphere rather than direct danger.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧可以来自气氛而非直接危险。

intro.en: Scary is scare plus -y, with roots in Old Norse skjarr, timid.
intro.cn: scary 由 scare 加 -y 构成，根源是古诺尔斯语 skjarr（胆怯的）。

items.en: Skjarr meant timid.
items.cn: skjarr 意为胆怯的。

items.en: Skerren meant to frighten.
items.cn: skerren 意为使害怕。

items.en: Scary appeared as an adjective from scare.
items.cn: scary 作为 scare 的形容词形式出现。

items.en: Scary movies and stories became popular labels.
items.cn: 恐怖电影和恐怖故事成为流行说法。

items.en: Scary is common in informal and media English.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scary 常见于口语与媒体语言。

note.en: Scary is compared with similar spellings and with other fear adjectives.
note.cn: 把 scary 与形近词以及其它表示恐惧的形容词作比较。

entries.definition: a mark left by a wound
a cloth worn around the neck

normalIntro.en: Scary is the adjective made from scare.
normalIntro.cn: scary 是由 scare 构成的形容词。

normal.en: Add y to scare and change e to i before it.
normal.cn: 在 scare 后加 y 时，e 变成 i，成为 scary。

normal.en: A scary movie makes you cover your eyes.
normal.cn: 恐怖电影让你遮住眼睛。

normal.en: Scarier and scariest change y to i before the ending.
normal.cn: scarier 和 scariest 要把 y 变成 i 再加词尾。

normal.en: A scary thought is one you cannot shake off.
normal.cn: 可怕的想法是你甩不掉的念头。

normal.en: The dark can make an ordinary sound scary.
normal.cn: 黑暗能让普通的声音变得吓人。

abstract.en: Scary things show us where our courage ends.
abstract.cn: 可怕之物让我们看见勇气的边界。

abstract.en: A story can be scary without anything real being there.
abstract.cn: 故事可以吓人，即使没有真实的东西存在。

abstract.en: What is scary in the dark may be harmless in the light.
abstract.cn: 黑暗中可怕的东西在光下也许无害。

examples.en: That was the scariest film I have seen.
examples.cn: 那是我看过最恐怖的电影。

examples.en: It is scary to walk alone at night.
examples.cn: 夜里独自走路很吓人。

examples.en: The abandoned house looked scary in the fog.
examples.cn: 那座废弃的房子在雾中看起来很吓人。

dict_mnemonic.text: scare 加 -y 变形容词 scary，拼写时去 e 变 y；意为「让人害怕的」。

root: 由 scare 加 -y 构成，根源为古诺尔斯语 skjarr（胆怯的），核心义「引起恐惧的」。

sensesIntro.en: Scary means frightening, easily frightened, or eerie and unsettling.
sensesIntro.cn: scary 意为可怕的、胆小的，或令人不安的。

core.en: Something that makes a person feel fear.
core.cn: 使人产生恐惧的事物。

branches.en: The core sense of causing fear.
branches.cn: 引起恐惧的核心义。

branches.en: A person who is easily frightened.
branches.cn: 容易受惊的人。

branches.en: A strange atmosphere that creates unease.
branches.cn: 造成不安的怪异气氛。

branches.en: Both a threat and a mood can be scary.
branches.cn: 威胁与气氛都可能是可怕的。

branches.en: The feared object and the fearful person share the word.
branches.cn: 被怕之物与胆小之人共用这个词。

intro.en: Scary sits at the adjective end of the scare family.
intro.cn: scary 位于 scare 词族的形容词一端。

latinIntro.en: The family is Germanic, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 该词族属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.example: The scariness of the film surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影的恐怖程度让我们吃惊。
我们看了一部恐怖电影。
爷爷讲了一个恐怖故事。

definition_en: to throw things over an area or to make a group move apart
core_image: 一阵风把桌上的纸页吹得漫天飞舞，四处落下
scene: 风把桌上的纸张吹得四散。The wind scattered the papers across the desk.
sceneCN: 这里 scatter 是「使散开」（第 2 个义项）；句意：风把纸张吹散在桌上。

senses.title: Throw over an area
senses.definition: to throw small things over a surface or area
senses.definitionCN: 把小东西抛撒在一个表面或区域上
senses.example: She scattered seeds across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她把种子撒遍田地。
senses.why: The concrete sense is distributing small objects widely.
senses.whyCN: 具体义是把小物件广泛分布。

senses.title: Drive a group apart
senses.definition: to make a group of people or animals move in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 使一群人或动物朝不同方向散开
senses.example: The police scattered the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 警察驱散了人群。
senses.why: Objects spreading apart become people driven apart.
senses.whyCN: 物件四散引申为人被驱散。

senses.title: Break up and spread
senses.definition: to separate and move in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 分开并朝不同方向移动
senses.example: The birds scattered when the cat appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 猫一出现，鸟群就散开了。
senses.why: The group itself can do the scattering.
senses.whyCN: 群体自身也可以执行散开的动作。

senses.title: Spread out data
senses.definition: to spread points or values over an area in statistics
senses.definitionCN: 在统计中把点或数值分散到某个区域
senses.example: The graph shows how the data scatter.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示了数据如何分散。
senses.why: The visual spread of points is called scatter.
senses.whyCN: 点的视觉分布被称为散点。

intro.en: Scatter is a Middle English word, perhaps related to shatter.
intro.cn: scatter 是中古英语词，可能与 shatter 有关。

items.en: A related form meant to disperse or sprinkle.
items.cn: 相关形式意为分散或撒播。

items.en: Scateren meant to throw about in all directions.
items.cn: scateren 意为向四面八方抛撒。

items.en: Scatter became common for crowds and seeds.
items.cn: scatter 广泛用于人群和种子。

items.en: Statistics adopted scatter for spread-out data.
items.cn: 统计学用 scatter 表示分散的数据。

items.en: Scatter covers physical, social, and statistical spread.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scatter 涵盖物理、社会与统计上的分散。

note.en: Scatter is compared with similar spellings and with words for spreading.
note.cn: 把 scatter 与形近词以及表示分散的词作比较。

entries.definition: to spread over a wide area
to scatter small drops or pieces

normalIntro.en: Scatter is the sound of small things flying apart.
normalIntro.cn: scatter 听起来就像小东西四散飞开。

normal.en: Scatter and shatter both suggest something breaking apart.
normal.cn: scatter 与 shatter 都暗示东西散裂。

normal.en: Sow seeds by scattering them over the soil.
normal.cn: 把种子撒在土壤上就是播种。

normal.en: The double t appears in scattered and scattering.
normal.cn: scattered 和 scattering 中有双写 t。

normal.en: Scatter the crowd means make it break up.
normal.cn: scatter the crowd 意为让人群散开。

normal.en: A scatter of houses means houses spread far apart.
normal.cn: a scatter of houses 意为房屋稀疏散布。

abstract.en: Scattering turns a single group into many directions.
abstract.cn: 分散把一个整体变成许多方向。

abstract.en: Ideas scatter more easily than seeds.
abstract.cn: 思想比种子更容易撒播。

abstract.en: What is scattered may never come back together.
abstract.cn: 散开的东西也许再也不会聚拢。

examples.en: He scattered the papers over the floor.
examples.cn: 他把纸张撒了一地。

examples.en: The wind scattered the leaves along the road.
examples.cn: 风把树叶吹散在路旁。

examples.en: The crowd scattered when the rain began.
examples.cn: 雨一开始，人群就散开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: scatter 与 shatter 形近，都含「散裂」之意；可记「一撒手，东西四散」。

root: 中古英语 scateren，可能与 shatter 同源，核心义「向四面八方抛撒、散开」。

sensesIntro.en: Scatter means to throw things widely, drive a group apart, spread out, or spread data.
sensesIntro.cn: scatter 意为广泛撒播、驱散群体、散开，或分散数据。

core.en: To send things apart in many directions.
core.cn: 把事物朝许多方向分开。

branches.en: The core act of throwing small things widely.
branches.cn: 广泛抛撒小物件的核心动作。

branches.en: A group is forced to break apart.
branches.cn: 群体被迫分散。

branches.en: A group separates by itself.
branches.cn: 群体自行分开。

branches.en: Data points spread across a graph.
branches.cn: 数据点在图上散布。

branches.en: Thrown objects and moving groups both spread.
branches.cn: 被抛之物与移动的群体都会散开。

intro.en: Scatter forms adjectives, nouns, and technical terms.
intro.cn: scatter 构成形容词、名词与技术术语。

latinIntro.en: Scatter is Germanic in origin, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: scatter 源自日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.example: A scattering of leaves covered the path.
items.exampleCN: 小路上散落着零星的叶子。

items.example: My scatterbrain brother lost his keys.
items.exampleCN: 我心不在焉的弟弟丢了钥匙。

items.example: The scatter plot shows a trend.
items.exampleCN: 散点图显示出一种趋势。

definition_en: a place where something happens, a part of a play or film, or a view
core_image: 警戒线围起的街角，警灯闪烁，路人远远围观
scene: 事故现场很快被警戒线围住。Police soon arrived at the scene of the accident.
sceneCN: 这里 scene 是「现场」（第 2 个义项）；句意：警察很快赶到事故现场。

senses.title: Part of a story
senses.definition: a part of a play, film, or book in which events happen in one place
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、电影或书中在同一个地点发生事件的一段
senses.example: The opening scene takes place in a kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 开场场景发生在一间厨房里。
senses.why: The core sense is a staged unit of action.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个被呈现的动作单元。

senses.title: Place of an event
senses.definition: the place where something, especially an accident or crime, happened
senses.definitionCN: 某事尤其事故或犯罪发生的地点
senses.example: Reporters rushed to the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们赶到现场。
senses.why: The stage becomes the real place of action.
senses.whyCN: 舞台变成真实事件发生的地点。

senses.title: View of a place
senses.definition: a view of a place, especially a beautiful one
senses.definitionCN: 某地的景象，尤指美丽的景色
senses.example: The mountain scene was painted in soft colours.
senses.exampleCN: 山景被用柔和的色彩画了出来。
senses.why: A framed view resembles a stage set.
senses.whyCN: 被框住的景象就像舞台布景。

senses.title: Public outburst
senses.definition: a noisy or angry display in front of others
senses.definitionCN: 在他人面前吵闹或发怒的表现
senses.example: Please do not make a scene in the restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 请不要在餐厅里当众吵闹。
senses.why: A public display is like a drama performed for others.
senses.whyCN: 当众表现就像为他人上演的戏剧。

senses.title: Social world
senses.definition: a particular area of activity or group of people
senses.definitionCN: 特定的活动领域或人群圈子
senses.example: She knows everyone in the music scene.
senses.exampleCN: 她认识音乐圈里的所有人。
senses.why: A social world is a stage with its own players.
senses.whyCN: 社交世界就是有自己演员的舞台。

intro.en: Scene comes from Greek skene, a tent or stage building, through Latin scaena.
intro.cn: scene 经拉丁语 scaena 源自希腊语 skene（帐篷、舞台建筑）。

items.en: Skene meant a tent or the stage building.
items.cn: skene 意为帐篷或舞台建筑。

items.en: Scaena named the stage and what appears on it.
items.cn: scaena 指舞台及舞台上的呈现。

items.en: Scene named a division of a play.
items.cn: scene 指戏剧的一个段落。

items.en: Scene entered English as a stage unit.
items.cn: scene 以舞台单元之义进入英语。

items.en: Scene extends to real places, views, and social worlds.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scene 扩展到真实地点、景色与社交圈。

note.en: Scene is compared with similar spellings and with words for setting and spectacle.
note.cn: 把 scene 与形近词以及表示场景和景象的词作比较。

entries.definition: what can be seen from a place

normalIntro.en: Scene began as the stage building and spread to every kind of setting.
normalIntro.cn: scene 起初指舞台建筑，后来扩展到各种场景。

normal.en: A scene is a picture with action inside it.
normal.cn: 场景就是一幅包含动作的画面。

normal.en: The scene of the crime is the place detectives study.
normal.cn: 犯罪现场是侦探研究的地点。

normal.en: Behind the scenes means out of public view.
normal.cn: behind the scenes 意为在公众视野之外。

normal.en: Make a scene means act out anger in public.
normal.cn: make a scene 意为当众发怒。

normal.en: The music scene is the world of musicians and fans.
normal.cn: 音乐圈就是音乐人和歌迷的世界。

abstract.en: Life is made of scenes, and memory keeps only some.
abstract.cn: 生活由一个个场景组成，记忆只留下其中一些。

abstract.en: Every public scene has an audience.
abstract.cn: 每一个公开场面都有观众。

abstract.en: A stage and a crime site share the same word.
abstract.cn: 舞台与犯罪现场共用一个词。

examples.en: The final scene of the film was silent.
examples.cn: 电影的最后一场是无声的。

examples.en: Photographers gathered at the scene.
examples.cn: 摄影师们聚集在现场。

examples.en: He made a scene when the order was wrong.
examples.cn: 订单出错时他当众发作了。

dict_mnemonic.text: scene 原指希腊戏剧的舞台建筑，舞台上的每一段是场景，舞台下的真实地点是现场。

root: 源自希腊语 skene（帐篷、舞台建筑），经拉丁语 scaena 入英语，核心义「呈现事件的场所或片段」。

sensesIntro.en: Scene means a unit of a story, the place of an event, a view, a public outburst, or a social world.
